summary: Module 7 VERIFY: stress-tested the drafted postmortem (progress/postmortem-linkops.md). (1) Contributing factors read aloud: every subject is a system or a missing gate -- CF1 'The auth middleware did not reject falsy/empty Authorization headers' (not 'the developer'); CF6 'the worker and the API shared one SQLAlchemy pool'; CF8 'the ready check did not verify queue/worker liveness'. No factor names a person. (2) Remediation items executed-by-a-new-engineer test: R1 'Add integration tests for auth middleware covering empty string, null, undefined, and malformed JWT Authorization headers; assert 401' is directly executable with zero clarifying questions; R5 'Cap long_url at 2048 chars via Field(max_length=2048)' names the exact file, class, and mechanism; R3 names the exact token mechanism (INCR on invalidate, reject mismatch on read). None are 'improve testing' vagueness. (3) One lesson that prevents the most future incidents: 'A service is reliable only where its contracts are enforced by the system, not by attention -- when you change one layer, enumerate and re-verify every consumer of the state you just mutated.' Reasoning: across all ten bugs, the common disease is unenforced cross-layer contracts (auth header validity, cache freshness, unique codes, pool isolation, bounded input, queue liveness); each bug was invisible in its own layer and only became visible at a boundary. This one rule, absorbed by the team, covers every bug in the report. Timeline uses precise UTC timestamps (14:20 known-good, 14:22-14:32 attack window, 15:10 audit, 15:14 restore), not 'around midday'. Postmortem answers both 'what happened' AND 'what we change' via the R1-R10 table with owners and checkable outcomes -- it is a learning document, not an incident report.
evidence: progress/postmortem-linkops.md: blameless contributing factors (CF1-CF10), executable remediations (R1-R10 with owners), precise UTC timeline
No person named in any factor; remediations change system, not humans
One-lesson prioritization: enforce cross-layer contracts structurally
